title: Natural locally constant description of the constant abelian sheaf
statement: Let X be a topological space and A an abelian group, and suppose the category of abelian groups in the universe of A admits sheafification on the open site of X [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Let A_X be the constant abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. There exist additive equivalences e_U:A_X(U) ≃ LocallyConstant(U,A) for all opens U, including the empty open, such that for every inclusion V ⊆ U, every s ∈ A_X(U), and every x ∈ V, e_V(s|_V)(x) = e_U(s)(x). No irreducibility or connectedness assumption is made.

source.place: Definition 006W and Example 0081; source text read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/006W and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0081

proof.text: For every open U, form the abelian group L_A(U) of locally constant maps U → A, with pointwise addition and restriction by precomposition. The set-valued sheaf condition [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-maps-sheaf] gives pointwise gluing. The glued map is locally constant, addition commutes with gluing, and therefore L_A is an abelian sheaf.

Let P be the constant presheaf with value A and let c:P → L_A send a to its constant map. For an abelian sheaf G and a morphism phi:P → G, choose a cover on which any f in L_A(U) is constant, with values a_i. The sections phi(a_i) agree on overlaps: on nonempty overlaps the values are equal, and on empty overlaps the sheaf has a unique section. Glue them. Comparison on common refinements proves independence of the cover. Addition and restriction commute with the glued sections, by checking them locally. This defines an additive natural morphism psi:L_A → G with psi c = phi. This uses the sheaf gluing and uniqueness condition in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Concretely take the open fibres f^{-1}(a) as the cover. To check addition compare f, g and f+g on the common cover f^{-1}(a) ∩ g^{-1}(b), where additivity of phi gives phi(a+b)=phi(a)+phi(b); uniqueness of gluing gives the global identity. For restriction to V use the fibres V ∩ f^{-1}(a), and use uniqueness again.

Any other extension of phi agrees with psi on constant maps and hence on every locally constant f on a cover where f is constant. The uniqueness of sheaf gluing gives global equality. Thus (L_A,c) has the sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies it with the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The resulting component maps are additive equivalences and naturality gives the pointwise restriction identity in the statement, including for empty opens.
